minutes.headline: Commission approved two wetland projects and continued the Hickory Hills lake drawdown hearing to November 7.
minutes.summary: The Commission held three wetlands hearings, heard a DEP circuit rider on solar farm permitting, and took an enforcement update. It voted orders of conditions for 46 Fire Road 12 and 611 Reservoir Road, and continued the Hickory Hills drawdown plan after long debate over Fish and Wildlife's objections. Members also discussed beach erosion enforcement, a Rob's Hill workshop, a bird-habitat grant application and a conference.

public_comment.topic: No comments from the public were offered at the opening.
Asked what a workshop on Rob's Hill would involve and how it would be structured.

votes.motion: Standard order of conditions for 46 Fire Road 12 with added conditions on erosion protection, waddles and at least three white pines, to be written once a revised plan is submitted
Continue the Hickory Hills drawdown hearing to the November 7th meeting, with the agent to work with the applicant on draft order conditions
Standard order of conditions for 611 Reservoir Road with the sand area below the cap of the wall and pitched away from the lake
Proceed with a grant application for the Hollis Hills property for the birds program through DCR
Reschedule the November meeting to the 28th

budget_items.what_was_said: The Sewer Commission funded the member last year and asked the Conservation Commission to split this year's cost. It covers registration, reception and one hotel night.
A member noted the cost of paying a contractor to remove fanwort mechanically, as a reason to keep drawdown as a tool.

decisions.decision: Hickory Hills hearing continued to the November 7th meeting, with the agent to draft order conditions with the applicant.
Fire Road 12 applicant to submit a revised plan with a storage area and a schedule before the order is written.
Commission agreed to schedule a workshop on Rob's Hill and a site visit, with dates to be set.
Commission agreed to cover part of the MMA registration cost with the Sewer Commission.

what_happened.line: The Commission continued the Hickory Hills lake drawdown hearing to the November 7 meeting, with the agent to work with the applicant on draft order conditions.
It voted a standard order of conditions for 46 Fire Road 12, with added erosion, waddle and white pine conditions, to be written once a revised plan is submitted.
It voted a standard order of conditions for 611 Reservoir Road, with the sand area kept below the wall cap and pitched away from the lake.
Members agreed to schedule a Rob's Hill workshop and site visit, with dates to be set, and to share part of a conference registration cost with the Sewer Commission.
The minutes record a grant application for the Hollis Hills property and a move of the November meeting to the 28th, but the votes were not audible.

why_it_matters: The Hickory Hills drawdown decision affects how the lake is managed for weeds, and the minutes note that mechanical removal by a contractor is a cost the drawdown tool can avoid.
The two orders of conditions set the terms for shoreline and buffer-zone work on private property near water, and they apply to the permitted work at those addresses.
watch_next: The Hickory Hills drawdown hearing resumes at the November 7 meeting, with draft order conditions expected.
The minutes record the November meeting moved to the 28th, but that vote was not audible, so check the posted agenda for the date.
